newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares end up, focus on BPI, Inparsa.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares end up, focus on BPI, Inparsa.

text.p: 1755 GMT - Portuguese shares ended firmer, but off the highs of the session, in turnover of 10 billion escudos, slightly above the recent daily average. More than 1.1 percent of the capital of BPI-SGPS was traded on the bourse today. Figest, personal holding of businessman Belmiro de Azevedo, said it had acquired on Lisbon bourse a stake of 4.4 percent in Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) that had been held by French bank Credit Lyonnais.

* On its first day on the bourse, 1.7 percent of the capital of Inparsa was traded. Inparsa traded around 1,300-1,400 escudos, in line with expectations. Inparsa, which has a capital of 19.5 billion escudos, combines the wood products businesses of Sonae Industria and the media, computing and tourism businesses of Pargeste.
* Dealers expected uncertainty to return to the market on Monday ahead of the U.S. rates decision on Tuesday. Investors may be reluctant to take positions and the session could be calm, they said.
